CHIEF COMPLAINT
Bilateral knee pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Andrew is a 62-year-old male with a past medical history significant for kidney transplant, hypothyroidism, and arthritis who presents with complaints of bilateral knee pain. The patient reports that over the weekend he was moving boxes up and down basement stairs. By the end of the day, both knees were painful and equally affected. He denies specific traumatic injury but notes a history of prior knee problems, attributing the current pain to repetitive activity and weight of boxes. The pain was significant enough to disrupt his sleep Saturday night. He has tried acetaminophen and ice without significant relief. He denies fever, chills, muscle aches, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. The pain has been affecting his activities.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies fever, chills, muscle aches, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Denies headaches. Reports occasional elbow pain but nothing out of the ordinary. No other symptoms reported.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
- Kidney transplant (several years ago for polycystic kidney disease)
- Hypothyroidism
- Arthritis

MEDICATIONS
- Immunosuppressive medications (for kidney transplant)
- Synthroid (for hypothyroidism)

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not documented.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: No fever, heart rate normal, blood pressure normal. Cardiovascular: 2/6 systolic ejection murmur appreciated, stable compared to prior exams. Knees: Right knee demonstrates edema and erythema with pain to palpation and decreased range of motion. Left knee appears normal without edema or erythema.

RESULTS
Right knee X-ray: Good bony alignment with no acute fracture. Laboratory results: White blood cell count not elevated (patient is immunocompromised). Kidney function very good.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Acute exacerbation of arthritis of bilateral knees with right knee more symptomatic: Start Ultram 50 mg every 6 hours as needed. Order autoimmune panel. Advise patient to take it easy. If symptoms continue, will consider further imaging and possible referral to physical therapy.
2. Hypothyroidism: Continue Synthroid. Order thyroid panel.
3. Arthritis: Continue current management. Note that patient cannot take certain anti-inflammatory medications due to kidney transplant. Will reassess in a few weeks and consider physical therapy referral if needed.
